blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Service gives something one stable name inside the cluster. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: Here the name points to a website outside the cluster instead of to Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Service, from the core v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.what: This Service is called academy-site. Pods in the namespace can look it up by that name.
blocks.why: Apps use the inside name, so the outside address can change in one place.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: academy-site

blocks.title: Point outside
blocks.what: ExternalName tells cluster DNS to answer with an outside name instead of an address.
blocks.why: No Pods and no ports are involved. Cluster DNS does all the work.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Service becomes ClusterIP and needs Pods and ports instead.
blocks.comment: Answer lookups with an outside name
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: academy-site
spec:
  type: ExternalName

blocks.title: The outside name
blocks.what: externalName is the DNS name to answer with: avizacademy.com.
blocks.why: Some websites reject requests sent to a name they do not expect. HTTP and HTTPS often fail this way.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Service, because an ExternalName needs a name to point to.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: academy-site
spec:
  type: ExternalName
  externalName: avizacademy.com

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Services are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Service gives something one stable name.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The inside name. Pods look it up as academy-site.
notes.spec: The desired state: what the name should point to.
notes.spec.type: ExternalName makes cluster DNS answer with an outside name. No Pods are selected.
notes.spec.externalName: The outside DNS name to answer with. Write a name only, without https://.

tryIt.result: TYPE shows ExternalName and EXTERNAL-IP shows avizacademy.com. There is no CLUSTER-IP.
Shows canonical name = avizacademy.com. Cluster DNS answers with the outside name.

questions.question: What does a Pod get when it looks up academy-site?
questions.explain: Cluster DNS answers with the outside name. The Pod then looks that name up as usual.

questions.question: Does this Service send traffic to any Pods?
answers: No, it has no selector and only answers name lookups
questions.explain: An ExternalName Service only answers DNS lookups. No traffic passes through it.

questions.question: Why use academy-site instead of writing avizacademy.com in every app?
answers: If the address changes, you edit one Service instead of every app
questions.explain: Apps keep using the same inside name. Only the Service changes when the outside address does.

fix.message: The Service "academy-site" is invalid: spec.externalName: Invalid value: "https://avizacademy.com": a lowercase RFC 1123 subdomain must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters, '-' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'example.com', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*')
fix.explain: externalName takes a DNS name only. https:// belongs to a web address, not to a name.
